name: qwen2_5_0p5b
description: Qwen2.5-0.5B, the model this fabric is sized to host. 494 MB of int8 weights against 1 GB of DDR3L on a Zybo Z7-20 leaves real headroom, where Qwen3-0.6B at 596 MB leaves little and a 1B model does not fit.
notes: Qwen2.5-0.5B: 24 layers, hidden 896, intermediate 4864, 14 query heads over 2 key/value heads. The heavy grouped-query ratio, 7 to 1, is why its KV cache is small for its size, which matters more on a 1 GB board than the parameter count does.
d_ff 4864 is the longest reduction, so the accumulator is 8 + 8 + ceil(log2(4864)) = 29 bits. Every block re-derives from that: nothing here is written for a particular model.

494 MB of int8 weights on 1 GB of DDR3L. Batch-1 decode reads all of them per token, so one board at 2 GB/s sustained is bounded near 4 tokens/s and two boards splitting the weights near 8. That ceiling is memory bandwidth: the MAC chiplet is idle most of the time and adding arithmetic does not move it.
Megatron tensor parallelism: QKV and the gate/up projections are column-parallel, the output and down projections row-parallel, so each layer ends with one all-reduce of a [1, d_model] activation.
